messages.content: The Boise tournament schedule is finally out. First match is 7:30 Saturday in Meridian, and if they make the final Sunday it could be midafternoon. The Hampton hold expires tonight. Do I keep that or switch to the Boise Bench hotel with better dinner options?

Keep the Meridian Hampton. The 7:30 Saturday match makes location and breakfast more valuable than late-Friday restaurant choices, and the Bench option adds drive time before the earliest match while dropping included breakfast. The clean plan is to eat before you get to Boise, then arrive late and go straight to bed.
That was my instinct. We can do dinner in Burley or Twin Falls. I mainly need to lock it without missing some room detail.

Book the cancellable two-queen room for Friday and Saturday. Add a late-arrival note saying you expect to arrive around 10:45 to 11:15 p.m. Friday and to keep the room held. Confirm these before paying: two queen beds, breakfast start time, free parking, cancellation deadline, and whether noon checkout can be requested for Sunday.
It is two adults and one teen, so two queens. Breakfast says 6 to 10 online, but with a 7:30 match we need it to actually be open at 6.

Call the front desk after booking and ask: Does breakfast open at 6 a.m. on Saturdays, and can we grab something right at opening? If they hedge, plan on hotel coffee plus road snacks and a later meal after the first match. Parking is listed as free, so you should not need downtown-style parking receipts for the stay.
If Sunday finals go until 3, can we keep the room or is that unrealistic?

Do not count on keeping the room until midafternoon. Ask for free noon checkout, maybe 1 p.m. if they can do it, but pack the car before the first Sunday match. Use the lobby restroom after checkout if needed, keep uniforms/snacks accessible in the car, and leave from the courts once play ends.
Great. Give me the final booking note I can paste into my file.

Book Hampton Meridian for Friday and Saturday, cancellable two-queen room, no prepay if avoidable. Add late-arrival note for Friday around 10:45 to 11:15 p.m. Confirm breakfast really starts at 6 a.m. Saturday, parking is free, and request noon checkout for Sunday. Eat dinner on the road Friday because nearby late options are limited. Sunday: pack car before matches, check out by noon unless the hotel grants later, use lobby restroom if finals run long, fuel in Meridian, and drive home after elimination or the final.

messages.content: I’m starting the Denver admissions conference planning now. It is Monday June 24 through Wednesday June 26 near the convention center. Monday has an afternoon committee meeting, Tuesday is full sessions, and Wednesday has a closing lunch. Can you compare Sunday versus Monday arrival and the hotel block versus nearby options? I’d also like to know if I can skip a rental car.

Yes. Two details affect the recommendation: what time does the Monday committee meeting start, and is there a hotel reimbursement cap before taxes? Also, are you checking a bag or just doing carry-on?
Committee meeting is at 2 p.m., but they may open the room around noon for badge pickup and informal table work. Hotel cap is $235 before taxes. Carry-on only.

Then Sunday is the safer arrival. For SLC to Denver, there are plenty of nonstops. A Sunday afternoon option around 1:45 to 3:18 gives you time to reach downtown, check in, and get dinner. A Monday morning arrival before 10 looks cheaper, but a modest delay would squeeze badge pickup, lunch, and the 2 p.m. meeting. No layover is needed on this route.
How tight is Monday really if I land before 10?

It works only if everything behaves. Land around 9:55, take the train or rideshare, reach downtown around 11:00 to 11:30, drop your bag, then badge pickup. A 45-minute flight delay or slow train connection turns it into a rushed arrival with no real lunch buffer. If the noon room opening matters, arrive Sunday.
Let’s price it assuming Sunday night, then. The venue is by the convention center.

Shortlist: official conference block at the closest hotel, about $221 before taxes, no included breakfast, expensive parking but irrelevant if you skip a car, best for stepping back between sessions. Hampton downtown/convention center area, about $205 to $218, breakfast included, roughly a 7 to 9 minute walk, good practical choice. Element or Hyatt Place downtown edge, around $189 to $205, breakfast likely included depending on rate, but more like a 12 to 16 minute walk or quick ride. All should stay under the room cap before taxes if the quoted rates hold.
I really do not want a rental car downtown. Is the airport train reasonable on a Sunday afternoon?

Yes, I’d skip the rental car. The A Line from DEN to Union Station is predictable and much cheaper than parking. From Union Station you can take a short rideshare to the hotel, or light rail/free downtown shuttle if the timing is easy. If you are tired, a rideshare all the way from the airport is simpler but usually much more expensive.
What do meals look like if I use the official hotel and there is no breakfast?

For the block hotel, assume paid coffee/breakfast unless the conference agenda lists morning food. Build in two quick breakfasts: one grab-and-go nearby or lobby café on Tuesday, and one before Wednesday sessions. For dinner, downtown is easy enough without a car: convention center, theater district, and Larimer area all have options within a short walk or rideshare. Sunday dinner is the only meal you need to plan intentionally after travel.
I can live without included breakfast if the block saves me from walking back and forth in dress shoes. I just do not want accounting to push back.

The block rate under $235 before taxes is the cleanest reimbursement story. Since you will not have parking, the only extras to watch are breakfast and any destination or facility fee. If meals are reimbursed separately or covered by per diem, the lack of breakfast matters less. I would keep the block hotel as first choice and the Hampton as the practical backup.
Can I hold both for a day or two while I confirm the agenda food?

You can if both are refundable and you calendar the cancellation dates, but I would not let duplicate holds sit long. If the conference block requires a card guarantee and has an earlier cutoff, hold that first. Then hold Hampton only if it has no prepay and a flexible cancellation. Put a reminder 48 hours before the earliest deadline to release one.
Okay. First choice is the official block, backup Hampton. Arrival Sunday. What outbound flight time would you hold?

Hold the Sunday nonstop around 1:45 p.m. from Salt Lake, arriving Denver around 3:18. It gives more buffer than a later afternoon flight and still does not eat the whole day. If that fare jumps, a midafternoon Southwest or United nonstop is fine, but avoid arriving so late that dinner and check-in become the whole evening. Select a window seat if the fare allows seat choice; if it is Southwest, set a check-in reminder.
Return Wednesday after the closing lunch, but not too late if I can avoid it.

I’d avoid anything around 3:25 unless you are willing to leave lunch promptly and already have your bag. A 4:40 or 4:45 nonstop is the best balance: enough time to leave downtown, get to DEN, and clear security without wasting the evening. A 6:15-ish return is safer if you expect post-lunch conversations.
Put the booking and reimbursement notes together. No rental car.

Denver plan: arrive Sunday June 23 on a nonstop SLC-DEN around 1:45 to 3:18; return Wednesday June 26 on a nonstop around 4:40 to 4:45 after the closing lunch. Hold the official conference block first if it is about $221 before taxes and refundable; hold Hampton downtown/convention center only as a short backup if flexible. Skip the rental car. Use A Line plus short rideshare or local transit downtown; keep rideshare receipts if used. Meal plan: Sunday dinner downtown, verify whether Tuesday/Wednesday conference mornings include coffee or breakfast, otherwise budget quick paid breakfasts. Reimbursement file: airfare receipt, hotel confirmation showing nightly rate under cap, hotel folio, train/rideshare receipts, meal receipts if applicable, and screenshots of cancellation deadlines and any hotel fees.

messages.content: Denver changed a bit. They added a Monday 11:15 roundtable, and the official block released one more room type but with a stricter cancellation date. The Hampton is still there, but Tuesday night jumped. Can you re-rank the plan?

With an 11:15 Monday roundtable, Sunday arrival moves from nice-to-have to the practical choice. Monday morning would be too fragile unless you were comfortable missing the roundtable. Send me the updated hotel rates and cancellation dates and I’ll rank them cleanly.

Official block is $219 before taxes, one queen room, cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. Hampton averages $226 now because Tuesday went up, cancel 48 hours before arrival. Element is $199 but farther from the venue.

Ranked now: 1. Official block, because it is closest, under the cap, and the Monday roundtable plus Tuesday full day make proximity useful. The trade-off is no included breakfast and the stricter June 14 cancellation. 2. Hampton, because breakfast is included and cancellation is easier, but the rate advantage is basically gone and you add walking. 3. Element, because it saves money but adds the most friction.
Breakfast is the only thing making me pause. I do not want to hunt for food before 8 a.m. sessions.

Use the block hotel and make breakfast boring on purpose. Check whether the conference provides morning coffee or continental breakfast. If not, buy yogurt, fruit, or bars Sunday evening and use one nearby coffee stop for Tuesday. That is less hassle than changing hotels for breakfast now that Hampton is almost the same price.
Good. What about flights? Still Sunday afternoon?

Yes. Hold the Sunday early-afternoon nonstop if it is still reasonable. The 1:45-ish departure is better than a later one because you can check in, pick up snacks, and have dinner without rushing. Monday morning should only be a fallback if Sunday fares become unreasonable.
Return Wednesday: closing lunch is listed as 12:15 to 1:15, but those things always linger. Is a 3:30 return risky?

Yes, 3:30 is skinny. You would need to leave lunch almost immediately, retrieve your bag, get to DEN, and hope security is smooth. A 4:45 return is much more comfortable if you leave downtown by about 2:15. A 6:10 return is the safety option if you expect a long debrief, but it costs you the evening at home.
No debrief planned. I want home before bedtime. Rank the exact version to hold.

Hold this version: official block one-queen room at $219, Sunday early-afternoon nonstop to Denver, Wednesday 4:45-ish nonstop back to Salt Lake, no rental car. Backup: same hotel and flights but a 6:10 return only if the closing lunch agenda grows again. Hampton is now only the backup if breakfast becomes confirmed as completely uncovered and inconvenient.
What deadlines do I need on my calendar?

Calendar June 14 at noon as the decision reminder, because the block cancellation is June 14 at 5 p.m. Also add a flight-price check within 24 hours of the hold, and a week-before reminder to verify conference breakfast, A Line timing, and whether the hotel has any extra destination or facility fee. If you briefly hold Hampton, set its cancellation reminder for 48 hours before arrival.
One more detail: the block room is one queen, not two. That is fine for just me, right?

Yes, one queen is fine for this solo trip. Before booking, confirm the room is refundable until June 14 at 5 p.m., the $219 rate is before taxes and within the cap, and there is no required parking or resort-style fee. Final Denver lean: book the official block, arrive Sunday afternoon, return Wednesday around 4:45, skip the car, and handle breakfast with conference food plus simple grab-and-go backup.
